A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAS-Orchestra and MASBENCH. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MASBENCH experiments, evaluations on five public benchmarks, ablations and case studies in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds LLM-orchestrator baseline results and quantitative inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The holistic function-calling procedure, low/high DoM constraints, GRPO objective, orchestration prompts and parser are unchanged. SearchAgent is renamed DeepResearchAgent in parts of v3 without a documented change to its workflow.

E1.justification: Both retain the same five MASBENCH axes, iGSM/RULER sources, DeepScaleR training data and five public evaluation benchmarks. Dataset statistics in Appendix A are unchanged; the added comparisons use existing tasks.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds a new comparator category, LLM as Orchestrator, evaluating GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 across all five public benchmarks. This substantially broadens the comparison beyond the retained standalone-agent and specialized orchestration baselines in v1 Table 4.

E3.justification: The new cost evaluation measures LLM calls, prompt-plus-completion tokens, dollar costs and wall time on AIME24 and GPQA. Existing accuracy evaluation, dataset splits, correctness judging and Table B.1 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused performance–cost analysis in Figure 1 and Appendix D.4. Existing adversarial-training, combined-training, orchestrator-size, context-length and agent-structure analyses and case studies are retained, often relocated to Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: Both versions report Avg@8 accuracy. v3 introduces no new seed or repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 accuracy rows and substantial new resource measurements in Table D.2, including AIME24 costs of $0.01 for MAS-Orchestra and $1.46 for AFlow. Matched earlier accuracy results remain unchanged, including MAS-Orchestra's 66.25 on AIME24 and 65.21 on GPQA.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the DoM formulation, five-axis definitions and GRPO optimization mathematics are unchanged. Expanded examples and the relocated optimization appendix introduce no new formal results.

C1.justification: v3 adds explicit claims of more than 10× efficiency and performance–cost Pareto optimality across its abstract, introduction and conclusion. The original contributions concerning holistic orchestration, MASBENCH and conditional benefits of MAS remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about baseline training-environment mismatch and implementation contributions to wall time, and attributes efficiency to adaptive delegation. It omits v1's qualification that the orchestrator directly supplied the easy NIAH answer in the illustrated robustness case.

D1.justification: Appendix D.4 newly documents Together AI pricing as the cost basis, asynchronous execution optimization and a planned full code release. Appendix C.6 additionally states the robustness training/evaluation ranges. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, parser and retrieval details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds an explicit xRouter reference and removes several citations, including Cemri et al. and Gao et al., with the earlier MAS-failure motivation. Core positioning against sequential orchestration remains; inference-time related work is relocated to Appendix E.

P1.justification: v3 separates the analysis framework from empirical research questions, rewrites boxed observations and takeaways as prose, consolidates and reorders appendices, and moves inference-time related work out of the main text. The public-benchmark narrative and conclusion are substantially compressed.

P2.justification: v3 adds the cost plot and resource table, redraws the framework schematic, expands Table 2 examples and adds result-table categories. It removes the configuration table while preserving its information in prose, relocates numerous diagnostic figures to appendices and revises plot labels and layout.

improvement.justification: The added strong-LLM comparisons and quantitative cost measurements strengthen empirical assessment beyond v1's qualitative efficiency discussion. Explicit environment and timing caveats also help interpretation. Sparse setup details for the added LLM baselines and removal of the robustness-case qualification limit the overall gain.
